root_idea.summary: The root has two closely related orientations: nullification or loss of efficacy, and painful swelling or obstruction, especially of the belly.
root_idea.development: The physical image is an animal becoming dangerously swollen after excessive or unwholesome feeding. From this developed the figurative use for deeds becoming void or unrewarded, as well as related uses for blood going without compensation and for wounds or water undergoing an adverse change.

qac_form_accounting.reason: Quran-attested Form I verb with a distinct intransitive use for deeds becoming null or ineffective.
Quran-attested Form IV causative verb for making deeds null or ineffective.

senses.definition: To become null, void, or ineffective of reward; to go for nothing.
senses.usage_conditions: In Quranic usage, the subject is commonly deeds or works. The use covers deeds that yield no benefit in the Hereafter, deeds performed without sincere intention, and good deeds whose opposing sins outweigh them; the emphasis is on loss of efficacy, standing, or reward.

senses.definition: To make deeds or works null, void, or ineffective of reward; to annul their reward.
senses.usage_conditions: A transitive causative use with deeds or works as the object. In the Quran it describes the nullification of the efficacy or reward of actions.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To become swollen or inflated, especially in the belly, through excessive eating or unwholesome pasture, with retention of what is inside; also, of the skin, to become swollen.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used of animals and people. In reference to a horse, the swollen flank or belly region is named rather than simply the horse.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of a wound, to leave scars or raised marks after healing, or to break open and become recurrent.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The marks may be scars of wounds or whips; the usage includes excrescent or swollen scar tissue.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of well water, to go away and not return as it was.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The intransitive and causative forms are both attested for this change in the water of a well.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of blood, to go for nothing, without retaliation or compensation by blood-money.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used of the blood of a slain person when no retaliatory claim or financial compensation is obtained.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To make a beast or a belly enter the swollen or obstructed condition called حَبَط.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: This is the primary causative physical use, distinct from the figurative causation of deeds becoming void.

other_classical_meanings.definition: For beating to leave a mark or scar upon someone.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The object is the person who bears the resulting mark or marks.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To cause blood to go for nothing, without retaliation or compensation by blood-money.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A causative use corresponding to the intransitive use of blood going unavenged or uncompensated.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To turn away from, avoid, shun, or leave someone.
Of a man, to be or become swollen or inflated in the belly; to be short and big-bellied; or to become filled with wrath, rage, or repletion.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The expressions for anger and repletion are recorded alongside the physical description and belong to this special derived form.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Swelling or inflation, especially of the belly, from excessive or unwholesome feeding; also a swelling of the udder or another part.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The swelling may be attributed to food, disease, or another cause; the term also denotes the condition in which the animal cannot void what is inside.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Scars or marks of wounds or whips remaining after healing, including raised scar tissue.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: This is a nominal use for the resulting scars or excrescent flesh, not for the swelling condition of the belly.

other_classical_meanings.definition: An animal whose belly is swollen or painful from excessive or unwholesome pasture and whose contents do not pass freely.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The word is also used of a horse swollen in the flanks.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The disease in which the belly becomes swollen or inflated from eating the herb ذُرَق.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: This names the disease condition rather than the verb or the animal experiencing it.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A short, big-bellied person; also one filled with wrath, rage, or repletion.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The supplied lexical discussion primarily describes a man; related feminine and variant forms are recorded separately in the tradition.
This is the feminine lexical specialization explicitly distinguished in the discussion of the related forms.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A man or child swollen or inflated in the belly; one filled with anger; one who becomes angry because something seems slow or late; or one who refrains in the manner of a seeker or desirer rather than one who refuses.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Several closely related physical, emotional, and behavioral uses are recorded for this active participial form.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Swollen or big-bellied; regarding something as slow or late; or cleaving to the ground.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: These uses are distinguished in the lexical comparison with مُحْبَنْطٍ.
